name: ZeroCloud Bucket
description: Keep your files stored and automatically synced across your devices.
introduction: We’re building Bucket as a shared collection that lives on the devices you choose. Each device keeps a copy, and changes follow you automatically.

overview.heading: Your files, wherever you pick up.

steps.title: Create a bucket
steps.description: Choose the files and folders you want to keep together.

steps.title: Connect your devices
steps.description: Keep encrypted copies on more than one device.

steps.title: Let changes follow you
steps.description: Automatic sync and conflict handling are central to the design.

note.title: A new phone. The same bucket.
note.description: The goal is to sync your collection back from another connected device when you replace a phone. Keep another complete, reachable copy so there is something to restore.

faqs.question: How is Bucket different from Share?
faqs.answer: Share hands a file to another device. Bucket keeps a persistent collection, stores copies on your devices and syncs changes between them.

faqs.question: Can I restore my files onto a replacement phone?
faqs.answer: That is a core use case. The new phone should be able to sync the bucket from another device that still holds a complete copy. The old phone is not the only place the data lives.

faqs.question: What happens if two devices change a file?
faqs.answer: Automatic conflict handling is a product requirement. Bucket is being designed to reconcile changes without leaving you to manage conflict copies; that sync system still needs to be built and verified.

faqs.question: Are the copies encrypted?
faqs.answer: Encryption for stored data and synchronization is a requirement from the start. Security belongs in the core design of Bucket, across every device that holds a copy.
